title: Inverse image commutes with extension of scalars, with its unit formula
statement: Let g:X→Y be a scheme isomorphism, O,O' commutative ring sheaves on Y_proet, α:O→O' a ring-sheaf map, and F an O-module sheaf. Use inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and extension of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is an isomorphism e:g⁻¹(O'⊗_O F)≅g⁻¹O'⊗_{g⁻¹O}g⁻¹F of g⁻¹O'-module sheaves. For V∈Y_proet, b∈O'(V), s∈F(V), e sends the module unit section of the sheafified pure scalar tensor b⊗s to the pure scalar tensor of the ring unit section of b and the module unit section of s. The unit-section and mixed-universe conventions are those of [def-pur-inverse-image-tensor-hom-sections].

source.place: Tags 03EK, 03EL, 03CY and 03D2; uniqueness of composite left adjoints

proof.text: Construct the scalar-extension functor by sectionwise tensor followed by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The ordinary extension/restriction-of-scalars Hom equivalence on each section, together with sheafification, gives its adjunction to restriction. The pushforward adjunction of [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-canonical-unit] has the recorded module-unit sections. The square of the two right adjoints commutes: both act identically on underlying sections, and ring-unit naturality identifies their scalar actions. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives e. Its unit identity proves the pure scalar formula for b=1. Express b⊗s=b•(1⊗s), use semilinearity of the module unit and linearity of e, and apply the same formula on X to obtain the assertion for every b. No flatness is used.
